clinical_features: Rapid onset of dyspnea at rest, marked orthopnea, cough with frothy/blood-stained sputum, tachypnea, severe hypoxemia, pulmonary crepitations and wheezing, S3 gallop, raised JVP, peripheral edema.
moh_protocol:
NON-PHARMACOLOGIC:
- Maintain open airway.
- Bed rest in sitting position (semi-fowler's).
- Oxygen via nasal catheter or face mask.
- Frequent vital sign monitoring.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- Furosemide 40 to 80 mg IV bolus stat.
- Refer immediately by ambulance.
urgent_referral_flags: Emergency medical condition -> Administer IV Furosemide, oxygen, keep patient sitting upright, and transfer immediately by ambulance to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 39

clinical_features: Breathlessness on exertion or lying flat (orthopnea), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea, night cough, lower chest crepitations, pitting pedal edema, ascites, tender hepatomegaly, raised JVP, S3 gallop.
moh_protocol:
NON-PHARMACOLOGIC:
- Salt restriction (<6g/day), weight reduction, avoid alcohol/smoking.

PHARMACOLOGIC (INITIAL THERAPY BEFORE REFERRAL):
- Diuretics: Furosemide 40 mg PO once daily or BID PLUS Potassium Chloride SR 600–1200 mg PO q12h.
- Spironolactone 25–50 mg PO daily (DO NOT combine with potassium supplements).
- Digoxin 0.125 mg PO once daily.
urgent_referral_flags: NYHA Class III-IV heart failure or worsening decompensation -> Start initial diuretic therapy and refer to hospital for specialized cardiac evaluation.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 40

clinical_features:
Asymptomatic in 90-95% of cases. Confirmed when SBP >= 140 mmHg and/or DBP >= 90 mmHg on 3 separate visits.
- Stage 1: SBP 140–159 or DBP 90–99 mmHg
- Stage 2: SBP >= 160 or DBP >= 100 mmHg
moh_protocol:
NON-PHARMACOLOGIC: Salt intake reduction (<1 tsp/day), 30min exercise 5-7 days/week, weight reduction, smoking cessation, alcohol restriction.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- First Line Monotherapy: Amlodipine 2.5–10 mg PO once daily OR Enalapril 5–40 mg PO daily OR Hydrochlorothiazide 12.5–25 mg PO once daily.
- Stage 2 Dual Therapy: Amlodipine 5mg + Enalapril 10mg PO daily.
urgent_referral_flags: Hypertensive Emergency (BP >= 180/120 mmHg with acute target organ damage: stroke, angina, pulmonary edema, eclampsia) -> Give Hydralazine 5-10mg IV or Furosemide 40mg IV stat and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 42

clinical_features:
Occurs 1-3 weeks after Group A Streptococcal throat infection in children age 5-15.
- Major Manifestations (Modified Jones Criteria): Migratory polyarthritis, Carditis/pancarditis, Sydenham chorea, Erythema marginatum, Subcutaneous nodules.
- Minor Manifestations: Arthralgia, fever, elevated ESR/CRP.
moh_protocol:
PRIMARY PREVENTION (Sore Throat): Procaine Penicillin 400,000–800,000 IU IM daily for 10 days OR Amoxicillin 500mg PO TID x 10 days.

SECONDARY PROPHYLAXIS (Prevention of Recurrence):
- Benzathine Penicillin G 1.2 million units IM (600,000 units if <30 kg) every 4 weeks.
- Duration: 5 years or until age 18 (without carditis); 10 years or until age 25 (with carditis); Life-long (with persistent valvular disease).
- Alternative (Penicillin allergy): Erythromycin 250 mg PO BID.
urgent_referral_flags: Active carditis, new heart murmur, or heart failure signs in a child -> Initiate secondary prophylaxis and refer to pediatrician/cardiologist.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 48

clinical_features:
Polyuria (frequent urination), polydipsia (excessive thirst), unexplained weight loss, blurred vision, recurrent skin/vulval infections.
- Diagnostic Criteria: Fasting Plasma Glucose >= 126 mg/dL OR Random Plasma Glucose >= 200 mg/dL OR HbA1c >= 6.5%.
moh_protocol:
TYPE 2 DIABETES:
1. Non-Pharmacologic: Medical Nutrition Therapy (avoid refined sugars, high fiber), 150min/week aerobic exercise.
2. First Line Oral Agent: Metformin 500 mg PO daily with meals (titrate up to 2000–2500 mg/day).
3. Dual Therapy (if target HbA1c <7% or FPG <130 mg/dL not met in 3 months): Add Glibenclamide 2.5–5 mg PO daily 30 min before breakfast.

TYPE 1 DIABETES:
- Insulin Regimen: Intermediate-acting (NPH) twice daily (before breakfast & bedtime) + Regular short-acting Insulin twice daily (before breakfast & supper). Total daily dose 0.2–0.4 units/kg/day.
urgent_referral_flags: Diabetic Ketoacidosis (DKA) / Hyperglycemic Hyperosmolar State (Kussmaul breathing, fruity breath, confusion, blood glucose > 300 mg/dL) -> Start Normal Saline IV infusion, give Regular Insulin 10 units IV/IM, and refer immediately to ICU.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 51

clinical_features: Excruciating sudden onset joint pain, redness, swelling, warmth. 80% of initial attacks involve the 1st metatarsophalangeal joint (base of big toe - podagra) or knee. Maximal severity within 12-24 hours.
moh_protocol:
ACUTE ATTACK MANAGEMENT:
- Rest affected joint, cold compresses, low purine diet.
- First Line NSAIDs: Ibuprofen 800 mg PO TID with meals OR Indomethacin 25–50 mg PO TID OR Diclofenac 50–75 mg PO BID for 5–7 days.

CHRONIC GOUT / MAINTENANCE (Start ONLY 2 weeks AFTER acute attack subsides):
- Allopurinol 100 mg PO daily (increase monthly by 100mg up to 300mg/day).
CAUTION: DO NOT start Allopurinol during an acute gout attack!
urgent_referral_flags: Suspected Septic Arthritis (single hot joint with high fever and systemic toxicity) -> Give analgesics and refer urgently for joint aspiration.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 57

clinical_features: Epigastric pain/burning, postprandial fullness, early satiety, heartburn, belching, nausea. Pain aggravated or relieved by food intake.
moh_protocol:
NON-PHARMACOLOGIC: Avoid offensive foods/drinks (spicy, greasy, alcohol, coffee, NSAIDs).

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- First Line PPI: Omeprazole 20 mg PO BID (or once daily) for 4–8 weeks.
- Alternative H2 Blocker: Cimetidine 400 mg PO BID x 4–8 weeks OR Ranitidine 150 mg PO BID x 4–8 weeks.
urgent_referral_flags: Alarm Indicators (Hematemesis/vomiting blood, melena/black tarry stool, progressive dysphagia, persistent vomiting, unintended weight loss, abdominal mass, age > 55) -> Refer urgently for upper GI endoscopy.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 61

clinical_features:
Internal: Painless bright red rectal bleeding with or following bowel movements, prolapse during straining.
External: Painful tender swelling at the anal verge.
moh_protocol:
NON-PHARMACOLOGIC: Fluid and fiber-rich diet, warm sitz baths 2-3x daily, avoid straining/constipation.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- First Line: Bismuth Subgallate compound suppository insert 1 suppository rectally BID OR topical ointment BID for 5 days.
- Alternative: Lidocaine + Zinc Oxide + Hydrocortisone suppository rectally once daily or BID x 5 days.
urgent_referral_flags: Grade IV strangulated, thrombosed, or profusely bleeding hemorrhoids -> Refer for surgical evaluation.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 63

clinical_features:
Fatigue, weakness, dyspnea on exertion, palpitations, lightheadedness, conjunctival/palmar pallor, tachycardia, koilonychia (spoon nails in iron deficiency).
- Diagnostic Threshold: Hb < 13 g/dL (men), Hb < 12 g/dL (women), Hb < 11 g/dL (pregnant women).
moh_protocol:
IRON DEFICIENCY ANEMIA:
- First Line: Ferrous Sulphate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO TID between meals for at least 3 months after Hb normalizes.
- Alternative: Ferrous Gluconate 325 mg PO 1-2 tabs TID.

MEGALOBLASTIC ANEMIA:
- Vitamin B12 Deficiency: Cobalamin 1000 mcg (1 mg) IM daily for 1 week, then weekly for 4 weeks, then 1 mg monthly for life.
- Folate Deficiency: Folic Acid 1 to 5 mg PO daily for 1–4 months.
CAUTION: Rule out Vitamin B12 deficiency BEFORE giving Folic Acid alone to prevent irreversible neurological damage!
urgent_referral_flags: Severe anemia (Hb < 7 g/dL) with heart failure, severe hypoxic dyspnea, or ongoing active hemorrhage -> Transfuse packed RBC/whole blood and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 67

clinical_features: Chronic fever (>1 month), chronic diarrhea (>1 month), unintentional weight loss > 10%, oral candidiasis/thrush, herpes zoster, persistent lymphadenopathy, recurrent bacterial pneumonia, TB co-infection.
moh_protocol:
DIAGNOSIS: National HIV Rapid Testing Algorithm.

FIRST LINE ART REGIMEN FOR ADULTS/ADOLESCENTS:
- Preferred FDC: Tenofovir (TDF 300mg) + Lamivudine (3TC 300mg) + Efavirenz (EFV 600mg) triple Fixed-Dose Combination once daily at bedtime.
- Alternatives: TDF + 3TC + Nevirapine (NVP) OR Zidovudine (ZDV) + 3TC + NVP/EFV.

PROPHYLAXIS FOR OPPORTUNISTIC INFECTIONS:
- Cotrimoxazole (TMP-SMX) 960 mg PO once daily for all patients with CD4 < 350 or WHO Stage 3/4.
urgent_referral_flags: WHO Stage 4 severe conditions (Cryptococcal meningitis, CNS Toxoplasmosis, Kaposi Sarcoma, suspected ART failure) -> Refer to Hospital ART Center.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 71

clinical_features: Gradual abdominal pain, lower cramps, bloody and mucoid diarrhea (10-12 stools/day), tenesmus, weight loss, low-grade fever. Stool exam shows E. histolytica trophozoites with ingested RBCs.
moh_protocol:
INVASIVE DISEASE / DYSENTERY:
- First Line: Metronidazole 500 to 750 mg PO TID for 5–7 days (Children: 7.5 mg/kg PO TID x 5-7 days).
- Alternative: Tinidazole 2g PO once daily for 3 consecutive days (Children: 50-60 mg/kg/day x 3 days).

ERADICATION OF CYSTS (To prevent relapse):
- Diloxanide Furoate 500 mg PO TID for 10 days.
urgent_referral_flags: Amebic Liver Abscess (fever, right upper quadrant pain, tender hepatomegaly) -> Refer urgently to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 81

clinical_features: Severe abdominal cramps, high fever, watery progressing to mucoid or bloody diarrhea, tenesmus. Stool microscopy shows abundant pus cells (leukocytes) and RBCs.
moh_protocol:
SUPPORTIVE: Rehydration with ORS / IV fluids.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- First Line: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 3–5 days.
- Alternative 1: Sulfamethoxazole + Trimethoprim (Cotrimoxazole) 800/160 mg PO BID for 5–7 days.
- Alternative 2: Ceftriaxone 1 to 2g IM/IV once daily for 3 days (Children: 20-50 mg/kg/day).
CAUTION: Antidiarrheal agents (Loperamide) are CONTRAINDICATED in bacillary dysentery!
urgent_referral_flags: Toxic megacolon, severe dehydration in infants, or persistent blood loss -> Give IV Ceftriaxone and refer to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 84

clinical_features: Abdominal cramps, bloating, nausea, anorexia, malnutrition, pallor (hookworm anemia), visible passage of adult worms in stool.
moh_protocol:
ASCARIASIS / HOOKWORM / TRICHURIASIS:
- First Line: Albendazole 400 mg PO single dose (Children 1-2 yrs: 200mg single dose) OR Mebendazole 500 mg PO single dose (or 100mg BID for 3 days).
- Alternative for Pregnant Women: Pyrantel Pamoate 700 mg PO single dose.

TAENIASIS (TAPEWORM):
- First Line: Praziquantel 600 mg (10 mg/kg) PO single dose OR Niclosamide 2g PO single dose.

GIARDIASIS:
- First Line: Tinidazole 2g PO single dose (Children: 50-75 mg/kg single dose) OR Metronidazole 250-500mg PO TID for 5 days.
urgent_referral_flags: Intestinal obstruction from heavy Ascaris burden or severe hookworm anemia (Hb < 5 g/dL) -> Transfuse and refer.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 95

clinical_features:
Pale (hypopigmented) or reddish skin patches with definite loss of sensation, thickened/enlarged peripheral nerves with tenderness, painless wounds or burns on hands/feet.
- Paucibacillary (PB): 1–5 skin lesions, single nerve trunk involved.
- Multibacillary (MB): >= 6 skin lesions or positive slit skin smear for AFB.
moh_protocol:
PAUCIBACILLARY (PB) LEPROSY (6 MONTHS TREATMENT):
- Rifampicin 600 mg PO once monthly (supervised) PLUS Dapsone 100 mg PO daily (self-administered) for 6 months.

MULTIBACILLARY (MB) LEPROSY (12 MONTHS TREATMENT):
- Rifampicin 600 mg PO once monthly (supervised) PLUS Clofazimine 300 mg PO once monthly (supervised) + 50 mg daily (self-administered) PLUS Dapsone 100 mg PO daily for 12 months.
urgent_referral_flags: Leprosy Reaction (Type 1 Reversal / Type 2 ENL: painful swollen nerves, red ulcerating skin lesions, sudden loss of nerve function) -> Give Prednisolone 40mg daily and refer urgently to leprosy specialist.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 102

clinical_features:
Uncomplicated Lower UTI (Cystitis): Dysuria, urinary frequency, urgency, suprapubic pain, cloudy urine.
Upper UTI (Pyelonephritis): Flank/loin pain, fever, chills, costovertebral angle tenderness, nausea, vomiting.
moh_protocol:
UNCOMPLICATED CYSTITIS IN WOMEN:
- First Line: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 3 days OR Norfloxacin 400 mg PO BID for 3 days.
- Alternative: Cotrimoxazole 160/800 mg PO BID for 3 days.

MILD/MODERATE PYELONEPHRITIS (OUTPATIENT):
- First Line: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 7–10 days.
- Alternative: Cotrimoxazole 160/800 mg PO BID for 14 days.

SEVERE PYELONEPHRITIS (INPATIENT):
- Ceftriaxone 1 to 2g IV once daily until fever subsides, then switch to oral Ciprofloxacin to complete 10-14 days.
urgent_referral_flags: Complicated UTI, UTI in men, pregnancy pyelonephritis, or sepsis signs -> Start IV Ceftriaxone and refer to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 163

clinical_features: Intense headache, high fever, vomiting, photophobia, nuchal rigidity (stiff neck), positive Kernig's sign, positive Brudzinski's sign, altered mental status (GCS < 14), petechial/purpuric skin rash (N. meningitidis).
moh_protocol:
EMERGENCY PRE-REFERRAL MANAGEMENT:
- Give immediate first dose of Ceftriaxone 2g IV (Children: 100 mg/kg IV stat).
- Keep airway open, give oxygen, control seizures if present with Diazepam 10mg IV.
- Refer urgently by ambulance to hospital.
urgent_referral_flags: Bacterial meningitis is a reportable medical emergency -> Administer IV Ceftriaxone immediately and transfer to hospital without delay.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 171

clinical_features: Sudden onset of involuntary motor movements, tonic-clonic convulsions, loss of consciousness, tongue biting, urinary incontinence, post-ictal confusion.
moh_protocol:
CHRONIC EPILEPSY MAINTENANCE (MONOTHERAPY):
- Generalized Tonic-Clonic: Valproic Acid 750–2000 mg/day PO in 2-3 divided doses OR Phenytoin 300–400 mg/day PO OR Carbamazepine 600–1800 mg/day PO.
- Absence Seizures: Valproic Acid OR Ethosuximide 750–1250 mg/day PO.

STATUS EPILEPTICUS EMERGENCY (Continuous Seizures > 5-15 min):
1. Secure airway, give oxygen, establish IV line.
2. First Line: Diazepam 10 mg IV over 1-2 minutes (repeat once after 5 min if no response).
3. Second Line: Phenytoin 20 mg/kg IV infusion at 50 mg/min.
4. Third Line: Phenobarbital 20 mg/kg IV at 60 mg/min.
urgent_referral_flags: Status Epilepticus refractory to Diazepam, new adult-onset epilepsy, or pregnancy with epilepsy -> Control seizures and refer to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 174

clinical_features: Productive or dry cough, upper respiratory symptoms (rhinorrhea), low-grade fever, wheezing or rhonchi on chest auscultation.
moh_protocol:
DRY COUGH SYMPTOMATIC:
- First Line: Dextromethorphan 15–30 mg PO TID to QID (Children 6-12 yrs: 7.5-15mg TID).
- Alternative: Codeine Phosphate 10–20 mg PO TID/QID.

PRODUCTIVE COUGH:
- Guaifenesin 200–400 mg PO QID.

BACTERIAL COMPLICATION (High fever, purulent sputum, diabetes/HIV co-morbidity):
- Amoxicillin 500 mg PO TID for 7–10 days.
urgent_referral_flags: Cough lasting > 2 weeks -> Rule out Tuberculosis (order sputum AFB smear / GeneXpert).
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 186

clinical_features:
Toxidrome Recognition:
- Cholinergic (Organophosphate/Pesticide): Excessive salivation, lacrimation, urination, diarrhea, vomiting, bronchospasm, miosis (pinpoint pupils), bradycardia.
- Anticholinergic: Dry skin, fever, tachycardia, dilated pupils, delirium.
- Opioid: CNS depression, respiratory depression, pinpoint pupils.
moh_protocol:
GENERAL MANAGEMENT:
1. Maintain airway, breathing, oxygenation, IV fluids.
2. Decontamination: Activated Charcoal 50g PO/NG tube diluted in 400ml water within 1 hour of ingestion.
CAUTION: Gastric lavage / vomiting is CONTRAINDICATED in caustic/corrosive or hydrocarbon ingestion!

SPECIFIC ANTIDOTES:
- Organophosphate / Carbamate: Atropine 0.5–2.0 mg IV stat, repeat q3-5min until bronchial secretions dry up.
- Opioids: Naloxone 0.4–2.0 mg IV push.
- Paracetamol: N-Acetylcysteine 140 mg/kg PO loading dose.
- Benzodiazepines: Flumazenil 0.2 mg IV.
urgent_referral_flags: Severe organophosphate poisoning requiring atropinization, organ failure, or persistent coma -> Administer antidote and transfer to ICU.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 214

clinical_features: Intensely itchy red papules and burrows in web spaces of fingers, wrists, axillae, belt line, and groin. Severe nocturnal itching. Family members usually affected.
moh_protocol:
TOPICAL TREATMENT (FIRST LINE):
- Permethrin 5% cream: Apply thin film to entire body from neck down, leave for 8–14 hours, then wash off. Repeat after 7 days.
- Alternative 1: Benzyl Benzoate 25% lotion: Apply neck to toe for 3 consecutive evenings.
- Alternative 2: Sulphur Ointment 10% (5% in young children): Apply for 3 consecutive nights.

SYSTEMIC TREATMENT (Crusted/Norwegian Scabies or Mass Outbreaks):
- Ivermectin 200 mcg/kg PO single dose.

ENVIRONMENTAL HYGIENE: Wash clothes/bedding in hot water or iron clothes after washing. Treat ALL household contacts simultaneously!
urgent_referral_flags: Secondary bacterial infection (superimposed impetigo/cellulitis) -> Treat with oral Cloxacillin 500mg QID before applying scabicides.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 292

condition: Syndromic Management of STIs (Urethral & Vaginal Discharge)
clinical_features:
Urethral Discharge in Men: Purulent discharge, dysuria.
Vaginal Discharge in Women: Abnormal quantity, foul odor, yellow/greenish discharge, vulvar itching.
moh_protocol:
URETHRAL DISCHARGE SYNDROME (GONORRHEA + CHLAMYDIA):
- Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO single dose (or Spectinomycin 2g IM) PLUS Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 7 days (or Erythromycin 500mg QID x 7d in pregnancy).

VAGINAL DISCHARGE SYNDROME (TRICHOMONIASIS + BV + CANDIDA):
- Metronidazole 2g PO single dose (or 500mg BID x 7d) PLUS Clotrimazole 200mg vaginal tab at bedtime for 3 nights.

PARTNER MANAGEMENT: Always notify, counsel, and treat sexual partners!
urgent_referral_flags: Treatment failure or persistent symptoms after 7 days -> Refer to STI clinic for culture and sensitivity.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 298

clinical_features: Foreign body sensation, redness, mucopurulent eye discharge, conjunctival follicular inflammation, tarsal scarring, entropion (inward turning of eyelid), trichiasis (eyelashes rubbing eyeball), corneal opacity.
moh_protocol:
WHO SAFE STRATEGY:
- S = Surgery for Trichiasis (TT).
- A = Antibiotics for active infection.
- F = Facial cleanliness.
- E = Environmental sanitation.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- First Line Topical: Tetracycline 1% eye ointment applied BID for 6 weeks.
- First Line Systemic (Mass Treatment / Intense Trachoma): Azithromycin 20 mg/kg PO single dose OR Doxycycline 100 mg PO daily for 3 weeks.
urgent_referral_flags: Trachomatous Trichiasis (TT) with eyelashes touching cornea -> Refer to cataract/trachoma surgeon for eyelid bilamellar rotation surgery.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 339

category: Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders (Chapter XVIII)
clinical_features: Pulsating ear pain worse at night, fever (39-40°C in children), hearing loss, ear discharge (otorrhea) following tympanic membrane perforation, mastoid tenderness.
moh_protocol:
ACUTE OTITIS MEDIA:
- First Line: Amoxicillin 500 mg PO TID for 10–15 days for adults (Children >6 yrs: 250 mg PO TID x 10d; Children <6 yrs: 125–250 mg PO TID x 10d).
- Alternative: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 625 mg PO BID for 10 days OR Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 7-10 days.
- Analgesia: Paracetamol 30–40 mg/kg/day PO.

OTITIS EXTERNA:
- Oxytetracycline + Polymyxin B + Hydrocortisone ear drops 2-3 drops 2-3x daily.
urgent_referral_flags: Swelling/redness behind the ear (Acute Mastoiditis), facial nerve paralysis, or severe vertigo -> Refer urgently to ENT specialist.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 344

clinical_features: Fever (often periodic), chills, rigors, headache, myalgia, nausea, vomiting, splenomegaly. Severe malaria: altered consciousness, severe anemia (Hb <5 g/dL), respiratory distress, hypoglycemia, jaundice, renal failure, convulsions.
moh_protocol:
UNCOMPLICATED P. FALCIPARUM:
- First Line: Artemether-Lumefantrine (Coartem) 20/120 mg tabs: 4 tabs PO at 0, 8, 24, 36, 48, 60 hours (total 24 tabs over 3 days).

UNCOMPLICATED P. VIVAX:
- Chloroquine 25 mg base/kg total over 3 days (10 mg/kg Day 1, 10 mg/kg Day 2, 5 mg/kg Day 3) PLUS Primaquine 0.25 mg/kg/day PO for 14 days (radical cure; check G6PD).

SEVERE MALARIA (PRE-REFERRAL):
- Artesunate 2.4 mg/kg IV/IM at 0, 12, 24h OR Artemether 3.2 mg/kg IM loading then 1.6 mg/kg daily OR Quinine 20 mg/kg IV in D5W over 4h.
- Treat hypoglycemia, control seizures, refer urgently.
urgent_referral_flags: Severe malaria (cerebral malaria, Hb<5, respiratory distress, renal failure, hypoglycemia, hyperparasitemia >5%) -> Give pre-referral artesunate and transfer immediately.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 85

clinical_features: Chronic cough >= 2 weeks, hemoptysis, night sweats, fever, weight loss, chest pain. Extrapulmonary: cervical lymphadenopathy, pleural effusion, spinal TB (Pott's disease), abdominal TB, TB meningitis.
moh_protocol:
DIAGNOSIS: Sputum AFB smear x2 or GeneXpert MTB/RIF.

NEW PATIENT (2RHZE/4RH):
- Intensive Phase (2 months): Rifampicin + Isoniazid + Pyrazinamide + Ethambutol daily (FDC by weight).
- Continuation Phase (4 months): Rifampicin + Isoniazid daily.

RETREATMENT (2SRHZE/1RHZE/5RHE):
- Add Streptomycin 1g IM daily first 2 months.

All TB patients: HIV test, DOT mandatory.
urgent_referral_flags: MDR-TB suspected (GeneXpert Rif-resistant), TB meningitis, massive hemoptysis, treatment failure -> Refer to hospital/MDR-TB center.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 108

clinical_features: Cutaneous: painless papule -> vesicle -> black necrotic eschar with edema; fever, lymphadenopathy. Inhalational: flu-like prodrome, severe dyspnea, shock. GI: severe abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea.
moh_protocol:
CUTANEOUS ANTHRAX:
- Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 7-10 days OR Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 7-10 days.
- Alternative: Amoxicillin 500 mg PO TID. Do not incise eschar.

INHALATIONAL/SYSTEMIC:
- Ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h OR Doxycycline 100 mg IV q12h PLUS additional agent. Urgent referral.

POST-EXPOSURE: Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID for 60 days.
urgent_referral_flags: Suspected inhalational, GI, or systemic anthrax; extensive cutaneous with systemic toxicity -> Start IV antibiotics and refer by ambulance.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Undulant fever, night sweats, fatigue, arthralgia (hip, knee, sacroiliac), hepatosplenomegaly, lymphadenopathy. Contact with cattle/sheep/goats or unpasteurized milk.
moh_protocol:
ADULTS:
- Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 6 weeks PLUS Rifampicin 600-900 mg PO daily x 6 weeks.

ALTERNATIVE (pregnancy/children):
- Cotrimoxazole 800/160 mg PO BID x 6 weeks PLUS Rifampicin.

PEDIATRIC: Cotrimoxazole 40 mg/kg/day TMP in 2 doses PLUS Rifampicin 15-20 mg/kg/day x 6 weeks.
urgent_referral_flags: Neurobrucellosis, endocarditis, large abscesses, relapse after two courses -> Refer for parenteral therapy.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Prolonged irregular fever, weight loss, massive hepatosplenomegaly, pancytopenia, hyperpigmentation. Endemic in lowland areas (Tigray, Amhara, SNNPR).
moh_protocol:
REFER TO SPECIALIZED TREATMENT CENTER.

FIRST-LINE:
- Sodium Stibogluconate (SSG) 20 mg/kg/day IV/IM for 30 days.
- Alternative: Liposomal Amphotericin B 3-5 mg/kg/dose IV, total 15-21 mg/kg.

HIV CO-INFECTION: Liposomal Amphotericin B preferred. Start ART + Cotrimoxazole.

SUPPORTIVE: Transfuse if Hb <5, nutritional rehabilitation.
urgent_referral_flags: All confirmed VL cases -> refer to treatment center. Severe anemia, bleeding, jaundice, HIV co-infection require urgent referral.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Intense pruritus, papular dermatitis (leopard/lizard skin), subcutaneous nodules over bony prominences, visual impairment progressing to blindness. Endemic near fast-flowing rivers in SW Ethiopia.
moh_protocol:
TREATMENT:
- Ivermectin 150 mcg/kg PO single dose, repeated every 6-12 months.
- Contraindicated in pregnant/breastfeeding women (first week), children <5 yrs or <15 kg.

NODULECTOMY: Excise accessible nodules.

MASS DRUG ADMINISTRATION: Annual/biannual Ivermectin in endemic communities.

SYMPTOMATIC: Antihistamines, emollients.
urgent_referral_flags: Ocular involvement (keratitis, optic atrophy) -> Refer to ophthalmologist. Severe Mazzotti reaction -> Corticosteroids and supportive care.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Sudden high fever (39-41°C), rigors, headache, myalgia, arthralgia, hepatosplenomegaly. Fever lasts 3-7 days then resolves, recurring 1-2 weeks later. Petechiae, epistaxis, jaundice in severe cases.
moh_protocol:
LBRF:
- Procaine Penicillin 400,000 IU IM single dose OR Doxycycline 100 mg PO single dose.
- Alternative: Tetracycline 500 mg PO single dose OR Erythromycin 500 mg PO single dose.

TBRF:
- Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 7-10 days OR Tetracycline 500 mg PO QID for 7-10 days.

JARISCH-HERXHEIMER: Common 2-4h after first dose (fever spike, rigors, hypotension). Give IV fluids and Paracetamol.
urgent_referral_flags: Severe Jarisch-Herxheimer with shock, DIC, myocarditis, hepatic/CNS involvement -> Resuscitate and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: S. mansoni: abdominal pain, bloody diarrhea, hepatosplenomegaly, portal hypertension. S. haematobium: terminal hematuria, dysuria, urinary frequency. Acute Katayama fever: fever, urticaria, eosinophilia.
moh_protocol:
TREATMENT:
- Praziquantel 40 mg/kg PO in 2 divided doses in one day (with food).

MASS DRUG ADMINISTRATION:
- School-age children in endemic areas: annual Praziquantel.

SUPPORTIVE: Ferrous Sulphate for anemia. Repeat treatment after 4-6 weeks if needed.
urgent_referral_flags: Hematemesis from portal hypertension, severe hepatosplenomegaly, urinary obstruction -> Refer to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Trismus (lockjaw), risus sardonicus, neck stiffness, dysphagia, opisthotonus, generalized tonic muscle spasms triggered by stimuli, autonomic instability. Incubation 3-21 days after wound.
moh_protocol:
1. Airway; may need tracheostomy.
2. Wound debridement.
3. TIG 3,000-6,000 IU IM.
4. Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h for 7-10 days (preferred) OR Procaine Penicillin 1.2 million IU IM daily x 10 days.
5. Diazepam 10-30 mg IV slowly, then 5-10 mg IV q1-4h as needed.
6. Tetanus Toxoid 0.5 mL IM.
7. Refer to ICU.
urgent_referral_flags: All tetanus cases are emergencies -> Administer TIG, Diazepam, Metronidazole, and refer to hospital ICU immediately.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Immunocompetent: often asymptomatic or mild lymphadenopathy, fever, malaise. HIV/AIDS: cerebral toxoplasmosis with headache, confusion, focal deficits, seizures. Congenital: chorioretinitis, hydrocephalus, intracranial calcifications.
moh_protocol:
IMMUNOCOMPETENT: usually self-limited.

CEREBRAL (HIV/AIDS):
- Pyrimethamine 200 mg PO loading then 50-75 mg/day PLUS Sulfadiazine 1-1.5 g PO QID PLUS Folinic acid 10-25 mg PO daily x >=6 weeks.
- Alternative: Cotrimoxazole TMP-SMX 10 mg/kg/day TMP in 2 doses x 6 weeks.

PROPHYLAXIS: Continue half-dose until CD4 >200 for >6 months on ART.

PREGNANCY: Spiramycin 1 g PO TID until delivery.
urgent_referral_flags: Cerebral toxoplasmosis with altered consciousness, seizures, focal deficits -> Start empiric treatment and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Epidemic (louse-borne): sudden high fever, severe headache, myalgia, macular trunk rash (spares face/palms/soles), confusion. Endemic (flea-borne/murine): milder fever, headache, maculopapular rash.
moh_protocol:
FIRST-LINE:
- Doxycycline 100 mg PO single dose (epidemic) or BID for 7 days (endemic).

ALTERNATIVE (pregnancy, children <8 yrs):
- Chloramphenicol 500 mg PO QID for 7 days.

SUPPORTIVE: IV fluids, Paracetamol.

PREVENTION: Delousing with Permethrin 1% dusting powder; wash clothes/bedding in hot water.
urgent_referral_flags: Severe epidemic typhus with DIC, gangrene, renal failure, myocarditis, CNS -> Start Doxycycline and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Low-grade fever, malaise, then pruritic rash starting on trunk: macules -> papules -> vesicles (dewdrop on rose petal) -> crusts. Lesions in all stages simultaneously. Highly contagious.
moh_protocol:
UNCOMPLICATED:
- Calamine lotion, Paracetamol (avoid Aspirin), keep nails short.
- Antibiotics only if secondary bacterial skin infection: Cloxacillin 250-500 mg PO QID x 7 days.

SEVERE/IMMUNOCOMPROMISED:
- Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x daily x 7 days (adults) or 20 mg/kg PO QID x 5 days (children).
- Severe: Acyclovir 10 mg/kg IV q8h x 7-10 days.

ISOLATION: Until all lesions crusted over.
urgent_referral_flags: Varicella pneumonia, encephalitis, neonatal varicella, or disseminated disease in immunocompromised -> Start IV Acyclovir and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Gradual onset joint pain worsened by activity and relieved by rest, morning stiffness <30 minutes, crepitus, bony enlargement (Heberden/Bouchard nodes), decreased range of motion. Commonly knees, hips, hands, spine.
moh_protocol:
NON-PHARMACOLOGIC: Weight reduction, low-impact exercise, physiotherapy, assistive devices.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- Paracetamol 500-1000 mg PO TID-QID (max 4 g/day).
- NSAIDs: Ibuprofen 400-800 mg PO TID OR Diclofenac 50 mg PO BID-TID.
- Topical: Diclofenac gel TID.
CAUTION: Shortest NSAID duration; avoid with renal impairment, GI ulcer, elderly.
urgent_referral_flags: Suspected septic arthritis (hot swollen joint with fever), severe deformity -> Refer to orthopedic specialist.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Localized lumbosacral pain; may radiate to buttocks/legs (sciatica). Red flags: bladder/bowel dysfunction, saddle anesthesia, progressive neurologic deficit, trauma, weight loss.
moh_protocol:
NON-PHARMACOLOGIC: Avoid bed rest >2 days, continue activities, physiotherapy, hot/cold packs, correct posture.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- Paracetamol 1 g PO TID-QID.
- NSAIDs: Diclofenac 50 mg PO BID-TID x 5-7 days OR Ibuprofen 400 mg PO TID.
- Muscle spasm: Diazepam 5 mg PO BID-TID x 3-5 days.
- Sciatica: Amitriptyline 25-75 mg PO at bedtime.
urgent_referral_flags: Cauda equina syndrome, progressive motor weakness, suspected fracture/infection/malignancy -> Refer urgently for imaging and surgical evaluation.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, fatigue, sleep/appetite changes, poor concentration, guilt/worthlessness, psychomotor retardation, suicidal ideation. Duration >=2 weeks.
moh_protocol:
MILD-MODERATE: Supportive counseling, psychoeducation, behavioral activation.

MODERATE-SEVERE:
- Amitriptyline 25 mg PO at bedtime, titrate to 75-150 mg/day.
- Alternative: Fluoxetine 20 mg PO every morning (max 40 mg).
- Continue >=6-9 months after remission.

SUICIDE RISK: Ask directly; if active plan, ensure safety and do not leave alone; refer urgently.
urgent_referral_flags: Active suicidal ideation with plan, psychotic features, or severe functional impairment -> Ensure safety and refer urgently to psychiatry.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Acute fever, productive cough, pleuritic chest pain, dyspnea, tachypnea. Exam: bronchial breath sounds, crackles, dullness over consolidation.
moh_protocol:
OUTPATIENT (MILD):
- Amoxicillin 500 mg-1 g PO TID x 5-7 days.
- Alternative: Erythromycin 500 mg PO QID x 7 days OR Azithromycin 500 mg day 1 then 250 mg daily x 4 days.

INPATIENT (MODERATE-SEVERE):
- Ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV daily x 7-10 days PLUS Azithromycin 500 mg IV/PO daily.
- Oxygen if SpO2 <90%, IV fluids, Paracetamol.

PEDIATRIC: Amoxicillin 40-90 mg/kg/day in 2-3 doses x 5 days. Severe: Ceftriaxone 50-80 mg/kg IV/IM daily.
urgent_referral_flags: Severe pneumonia (RR >30, SpO2 <90%, confusion, multilobar, septic shock) or no improvement after 48-72h -> Refer to hospital for IV antibiotics.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 188

clinical_features: Recurrent wheeze, cough (especially nocturnal), chest tightness, dyspnea. Triggered by allergens, cold air, exercise, infections. Bilateral expiratory wheeze, prolonged expiration.
moh_protocol:
ACUTE EXACERBATION:
- Salbutamol 2-4 puffs via spacer every 20 min x 3 OR nebulization 2.5-5 mg.
- Prednisolone 40-50 mg PO daily x 5-7 days.
- Oxygen to keep SpO2 >90%.
- No response: Aminophylline 250 mg IV slowly over 20 min.

CHRONIC (STEPWISE):
- Step 1: As-needed Salbutamol.
- Step 2: Beclomethasone 200-400 mcg/day inhaled BID.
- Step 3-4: Increase inhaled steroid or add long-acting beta-agonist.
urgent_referral_flags: Life-threatening asthma (silent chest, cyanosis, bradycardia, exhaustion, SpO2 <90%) -> Nebulize Salbutamol continuously, IV steroids, transfer immediately.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 190

clinical_features: History of submersion. Range: asymptomatic to cough, tachypnea, wheeze, frothy sputum, cyanosis, hypothermia, altered consciousness, cardiac arrest.
moh_protocol:
1. Remove from water; start CPR immediately if apneic/pulseless (prioritize ventilation).
2. C-spine precautions if trauma/diving suspected.
3. Oxygen, keep warm, remove wet clothes.
4. If breathing: recovery position, continuous monitoring.
5. IV Normal Saline for hypotension.
6. Pulmonary edema: Furosemide 40 mg IV.
7. Bronchospasm: Salbutamol nebulization.

Observe all patients 6-24h (risk of delayed pulmonary edema).
urgent_referral_flags: All near-drowning with respiratory symptoms, altered consciousness, or cardiac arrest -> Stabilize and refer to hospital for observation.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Tachycardia, hypotension (SBP <90), weak pulse, cold clammy skin, pallor, oliguria, altered mental status. Septic: fever/hypothermia. Anaphylactic: urticaria, angioedema, bronchospasm.
moh_protocol:
GENERAL:
1. Airway, high-flow oxygen.
2. Two large-bore IVs.
3. Rapid NS or RL 1-2 L bolus (children 20 mL/kg), repeat.
4. Trendelenburg position.

HYPOVOLEMIC: Control bleeding, transfuse if Hb <7.

SEPTIC: Ceftriaxone 2 g IV + Metronidazole 500 mg IV; identify/drain source.

ANAPHYLACTIC: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM thigh (1:1000), repeat q5-15 min; Hydrocortisone 200 mg IV; Chlorpheniramine 10 mg IV/IM.
urgent_referral_flags: All shock is a medical emergency -> Resuscitate and transfer immediately.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 210

clinical_features: Sudden unilateral weakness, facial droop, slurred speech or aphasia, visual loss, severe headache, altered consciousness, dizziness, dysphagia.
moh_protocol:
1. Airway, oxygen if SpO2 <94%.
2. NPO until swallowing assessed.
3. IV access, Normal Saline maintenance (avoid dextrose).
4. Monitor BP: do NOT aggressively lower unless >220/120 or hypertensive emergency.
5. Paracetamol for fever; Diazepam 10 mg IV for seizures.
6. Elevate head 30 degrees, lateral position.
7. Aspirin 300 mg PO/PR ONLY if hemorrhagic stroke excluded.

Refer immediately for CT scan.
urgent_referral_flags: All suspected stroke -> Stabilize and transfer urgently to hospital with CT. Thrombolysis window is 4.5 hours.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Hematemesis (fresh blood or coffee-ground), melena, hypovolemia (tachycardia, hypotension, pallor, cold extremities, oliguria). Causes: peptic ulcer, esophageal varices, erosive gastritis.
moh_protocol:
1. Airway, lateral position to prevent aspiration.
2. Two large-bore IVs; rapid NS/RL 1-2 L.
3. Cross-match blood; transfuse if Hb <7 or hemodynamic instability.
4. Oxygen, monitor vitals hourly, Foley for urine output.
5. Pantoprazole 40 mg IV or Omeprazole 40 mg IV BID.
6. Octreotide 50 mcg IV bolus then 50 mcg/hour if variceal bleed suspected.
7. NPO until endoscopy.

Urgent referral for endoscopy and definitive care.
urgent_referral_flags: Massive hematemesis, hemodynamic instability, recurrent bleeding, or suspected variceal bleed -> Resuscitate and transfer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 220

clinical_features: Follows streptococcal throat/skin infection by 1-3 weeks. Hematuria (cola-colored urine), edema (periorbital/pedal), oliguria, hypertension, fatigue, mild fever.
moh_protocol:
GENERAL: Restrict salt, monitor fluids, bed rest.

INFECTION ERADICATION:
- Phenoxymethylpenicillin 250 mg PO QID x 10 days OR Benzathine Penicillin 1.2 million IU IM single dose (600,000 IU if <30 kg).
- Penicillin allergy: Erythromycin 250 mg PO QID x 10 days.

HYPERTENSION:
- Hydralazine 0.25-1 mg/kg PO/IM q6-8h OR Nifedipine 0.25 mg/kg PO.

EDEMA:
- Furosemide 1-2 mg/kg PO/IV once daily (max 40 mg).
urgent_referral_flags: Severe hypertension (encephalopathy, seizures), oligo-anuric renal failure, hyperkalemia, pulmonary edema, or cardiac failure -> Refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Children 6 months-3 years. Barking cough, inspiratory stridor, hoarse voice, low-grade fever, respiratory distress. Often worse at night. Paroxysmal cold symptoms.
moh_protocol:
MILD (stridor only with agitation, no respiratory distress):
- Dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO/IM (max 10 mg) single dose.
- Supportive: cool-mist humidification, fluids, Paracetamol.

MODERATE-SEVERE (stridor at rest, respiratory distress, retractions, cyanosis):
- Dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO/IM/IV (max 10 mg).
- Nebulized Epinephrine 1:1000 (0.5 mL/kg, max 5 mL) via nebulizer, repeat q20min as needed.
- Oxygen to maintain SpO2 >92%.

All moderate-severe cases require observation and referral.
urgent_referral_flags: Severe respiratory distress, cyanosis, altered consciousness, or failure to improve after 4 hours -> Nebulize epinephrine, give Dexamethasone, and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Newborn <28 days. Fever or hypothermia, poor feeding, lethargy, irritability, respiratory distress, cyanosis, jaundice, hypotonia, convulsions, vomiting, diarrhea. May present with just one subtle sign.
moh_protocol:
ALL SUSPECTED NEONATAL SEPSIS NEEDS URGENT REFERRAL. Empiric pre-referral antibiotics:
- Ampicillin 50 mg/kg IV/IM q12h PLUS Gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV/IM q24h.
- Alternative: Ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IV/IM q24h (avoid if hyperbilirubinemia <2 weeks).

SUPPORTIVE: Keep warm, oxygen, IV fluids, glucose monitoring, breast milk feeding if tolerated.

MATERNAL RISK FACTORS: PROM >18h, maternal fever, foul-smelling liquor.
urgent_referral_flags: Any suspected neonatal sepsis -> Give first dose of antibiotics and transfer urgently to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Sudden onset choking, coughing, gagging, wheeze, stridor, dyspnea, unilateral decreased breath sounds. Often in children aged 1-3 years with history of eating/playing with small objects.
moh_protocol:
COMPLETE AIRWAY OBSTRUCTION (cannot speak/cry/breathe, cyanotic):
- Infants <1 yr: 5 back blows then 5 chest thrusts.
- Children >1 yr: 5 abdominal thrusts (Heimlich maneuver).
- Repeat until object expelled or patient becomes unconscious; if unconscious, start CPR.

PARTIAL OBSTRUCTION (able to breathe/cough):
- Allow patient to cough spontaneously, do NOT perform blind finger sweep.
- Oxygen, calm child, monitor closely.

All children with suspected aspiration require referral for bronchoscopy if object not expelled.
urgent_referral_flags: Complete airway obstruction, persistent respiratory distress, or radiopaque object in airway -> Attempt removal and transfer immediately to facility with bronchoscopy.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Children 6 months-3 years. Craniotabes, delayed fontanelle closure, rachitic rosary, Harrison's sulcus, wrist/ankle widening, bowing of legs (genu varum), knock-knees (genu valgum), delayed walking, irritability, growth failure.
moh_protocol:
TREATMENT:
- Cholecalciferol (Vitamin D3) 2,000 IU PO daily x 6 weeks OR 50,000-60,000 IU single oral dose (stoss therapy) under supervision.
- Calcium 500-1000 mg PO daily x 6 weeks.

PREVENTION:
- Vitamin A supplementation as per national schedule.
- Adequate sunlight exposure, calcium-rich diet, continued breastfeeding.

FOLLOW-UP: Monitor healing at wrists/knees after 6 weeks.
urgent_referral_flags: Signs of severe hypocalcemia (tetany, carpopedal spasm, seizures), or failure to improve -> Refer for pediatric evaluation.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: White curd-like plaques on buccal mucosa, tongue, palate, or oropharynx that can be scraped off leaving an erythematous base. Refusal to feed, irritability, drooling. Common in infants, immunosuppressed, or after antibiotics.
moh_protocol:
INFANTS/CHILDREN:
- Nystatin 100,000 units/mL suspension: 1-2 mL to each side of mouth QID for 7-14 days (after feeds).
- Alternative: Miconazole 2% oral gel 2.5 mL applied to affected areas BID for 7-14 days.

BREASTFEEDING MOTHERS: Treat nipple candidiasis with Miconazole cream BID.

RECURRENT/PERSISTENT: Consider HIV testing and Cotrimoxazole prophylaxis.

PREVENTION: Clean pacifiers/bottles; maintain oral hygiene.
urgent_referral_flags: Oropharyngeal candidiasis with dysphagia, immunosuppression, or failure to improve after 14 days -> Refer for systemic antifungal therapy.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Acute spreading infection of dermis and subcutaneous tissue. Red, hot, swollen, tender skin with poorly demarcated borders, often on lower extremities. Fever, malaise, regional lymphadenopathy. May follow a break in skin.
moh_protocol:
MILD (no systemic signs):
- Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 625 mg PO BID OR Cloxacillin 500 mg PO QID for 7-10 days.

MODERATE-SEVERE (fever, rapidly spreading, facial/orbital, diabetes/immunocompromised):
- Cloxacillin 2 g IV q6h OR Ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV daily.
- Add Metronidazole 500 mg PO/IV BID if anaerobic/necrotizing suspected.

SUPPORTIVE: Elevate limb, mark borders, warm compresses, analgesics.
urgent_referral_flags: Cellulitis around eye/face, rapidly spreading, systemic toxicity, bullae, necrosis, or no improvement after 48h -> Start IV antibiotics and refer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 283

clinical_features: Acute, well-demarcated, raised, bright-red, tender plaque with sharp borders. Common on face (butterfly distribution) and lower legs. High fever, chills, malaise. More superficial than cellulitis.
moh_protocol:
FIRST-LINE:
- Phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg PO QID for 7-10 days OR Benzathine Penicillin 1.2 million IU IM single dose.

ALTERNATIVE (Penicillin allergy or Staph suspected):
- Cloxacillin 500 mg PO QID for 7-10 days OR Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 625 mg PO BID for 7-10 days.

SEVERE (facial involvement, systemic toxicity):
- Procaine Penicillin 400,000-800,000 IU IM daily OR Ceftriaxone 1 g IV daily until afebrile, then oral to complete 10 days.

SUPPORTIVE: Elevate affected limb, Paracetamol.
urgent_referral_flags: Facial/orbital erysipelas, high fever with systemic toxicity, or no response after 48h -> Start IV antibiotics and refer to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 284

clinical_features: Superficial bacterial skin infection with golden/honey-colored crusted lesions, often around mouth and nose. Non-bullous form: vesiculopustules that rupture and crust. Bullous form: larger flaccid bullae, caused by Staph aureus.
moh_protocol:
LOCALIZED (few lesions):
- Mupirocin 2% ointment TID for 7 days.
- Gentle washing with soap/water and remove crusts.

EXTENSIVE OR SYSTEMIC SYMPTOMS:
- Cloxacillin 250-500 mg PO QID for 7 days (Children 25-50 mg/kg/day in 4 doses).
- Alternative: Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 25-45 mg/kg/day PO in 2 divided doses.

POST-STREPTOCOCCAL GLOMERULONEPHRITIS PROPHYLAXIS: Penicillin for contacts if outbreak.
urgent_referral_flags: Fever, rapidly spreading lesions, bullous impetigo, or suspected glomerulonephritis 2-3 weeks later -> Oral antibiotics and refer for complications.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 286

clinical_features: Itchy, erythematous, raised wheals with central pallor and well-defined borders. Each lesion lasts <24 hours. May be associated with angioedema. Triggers: foods, drugs, infections, insect stings, physical factors.
moh_protocol:
FIRST-LINE:
- Cetirizine 10 mg PO daily (Children 6-12 yrs: 5-10 mg; 2-6 yrs: 2.5-5 mg).
- Alternative: Chlorpheniramine 4 mg PO TID (sedating).

SEVERE/ANGIOEDEMA:
- Add Prednisolone 30-40 mg PO daily for 5-7 days.
- If anaphylaxis: Epinephrine 0.5 mg IM 1:1000, Hydrocortisone 200 mg IV, Chlorpheniramine 10 mg IV/IM.

AVOID: Known trigger; stop offending drug.
SUPPORTIVE: Calamine lotion, cool compresses.
urgent_referral_flags: Angioedema involving airway, dysphagia, stridor, hypotension, or anaphylaxis -> Epinephrine IM immediately and transfer to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 290

clinical_features: Painful or painless genital ulcer(s), inguinal lymphadenopathy, dysuria, vaginal/urethral discharge. Causes: syphilis, chancroid, genital herpes, lymphogranuloma venereum, donovanosis.
moh_protocol:
SYNDROMIC TREATMENT (cover common causes):
- Benzathine Penicillin 2.4 million IU IM single dose (1.2 million IU in each buttock) for syphilis.
- PLUS Azithromycin 1 g PO single dose OR Erythromycin 500 mg PO QID x 7 days for chancroid/LGV.
- PLUS Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 14 days (if LGV suspected; avoid in pregnancy).
- PLUS Acyclovir 400 mg PO TID x 7-10 days if vesicular/herpetic lesions.

PREGNANCY: Avoid Doxycycline; use Erythromycin.

PARTNER MANAGEMENT: Treat partners; promote condom use; test for HIV/syphilis.
urgent_referral_flags: Pregnancy with suspected syphilis, treatment failure, severe herpes with urinary retention, or signs of disseminated infection -> Refer to STI/HIV clinic.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 300

clinical_features: Lower abdominal/pelvic pain, fever, abnormal vaginal discharge, menorrhagia or intermenstrual bleeding, dyspareunia, cervical motion tenderness, adnexal tenderness. Caused by ascending infection from cervix (gonorrhea, chlamydia, anaerobes).
moh_protocol:
OUTPATIENT (MILD-MODERATE):
- Ceftriaxone 250 mg IM single dose PLUS Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 14 days PLUS Metronidazole 400-500 mg PO BID for 14 days.

INPATIENT (SEVERE, PREGNANCY, TUBO-OVARIAN ABSCESS):
- Cefoxitin 2 g IV q6h OR Ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV daily PLUS Doxycycline 100 mg IV/PO BID PLUS Metronidazole 500 mg IV/PO BID.

SUPPORTIVE: Analgesia, hydration, abstain from sex until treatment completed.

ALL PATIENTS: Test for HIV, syphilis, pregnancy.
urgent_referral_flags: Severe illness with high fever, tubo-ovarian abscess, pregnancy, or no improvement after 72h -> Hospitalize for IV antibiotics and rule out surgical abdomen.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 302

clinical_features: Sudden severe eye pain, redness, photophobia, blurred vision, tearing, blepharospasm after chemical exposure. Acid burns cause coagulative necrosis; alkali burns are more severe (liquefactive necrosis).
moh_protocol:
IMMEDIATE (TIME-CRITICAL):
1. Copious irrigation with clean water or Normal Saline for at least 15-30 minutes; remove contact lenses.
2. Use topical anesthetic (Tetracaine 0.5% drops) to aid irrigation.
3. Evert eyelids and sweep fornices to remove particulate matter.

AFTER IRRIGATION:
- Chloramphenicol 0.5% eye drops QID.
- Atropine 1% eye drops BID to prevent synechiae.
- Tetanus prophylaxis.
- Patch eye ONLY if small corneal abrasion; do NOT patch chemical burns.

ANALGESIA: Paracetamol.

Do NOT attempt neutralization with another chemical.
urgent_referral_flags: Any chemical eye burn, especially alkali (cement, ammonia, lye), severe pain, or vision loss -> Irrigate copiously and transfer urgently to ophthalmology.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 330

clinical_features: Sudden severe unilateral eye pain, blurred vision with halos around lights, headache, nausea/vomiting, markedly injected eye, steamy/cloudy cornea, fixed mid-dilated pupil, shallow anterior chamber. Tender, hard globe.
moh_protocol:
EMERGENCY PRE-REFERRAL TREATMENT:
1. Acetazolamide 500 mg PO/IV stat, then 250 mg PO QID.
2. Pilocarpine 2% eye drops 1 drop every 15 min for 2 doses, then 1 drop QID (constrict pupil).
3. Timolol 0.5% eye drops 1 drop BID (reduce aqueous production).
4. Mannitol 20% 1-2 g/kg IV if available.
5. Anti-emetic: Metoclopramide 10 mg IM/IV.
6. Keep patient semi-upright.

Urgent ophthalmology referral for laser/surgical iridotomy.
urgent_referral_flags: Suspected acute angle-closure glaucoma -> Start Acetazolamide + Pilocarpine + Timolol and transfer immediately to ophthalmologist (vision-threatening emergency).
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 334

category: Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders (Chapter XVIII)
clinical_features: Nasal congestion, purulent nasal discharge, facial pain/pressure (worse on bending forward), postnasal drip, cough, fever, hyposmia. Symptoms <4 weeks (acute).
moh_protocol:
MOST CASES VIRAL (symptomatic treatment):
- Saline nasal irrigation, steam inhalation, rest, fluids.
- Paracetamol for pain/fever.

BACTERIAL (symptoms >10 days, severe fever, purulent discharge, facial pain):
- Amoxicillin 500 mg PO TID for 5-7 days.
- Alternative: Doxycycline 100 mg PO BID for 5-7 days OR Cotrimoxazole 800/160 mg PO BID for 7 days.

DECONGESTANTS (short term only):
- Pseudoephedrine 60 mg PO QID for max 5 days OR Oxymetazoline nasal spray BID for max 3 days.

Avoid antibiotics in uncomplicated viral sinusitis.
urgent_referral_flags: Orbital/periorbital swelling, visual changes, severe headache, high fever, or symptoms >12 weeks (chronic) -> Refer to ENT/specialist.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 348

category: Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders (Chapter XVIII)
clinical_features: Bleeding from one or both nostrils. Anterior bleeds from Kiesselbach's plexus are common and usually minor. Posterior bleeds are heavier, often bilateral, more common in elderly/hypertensives.
moh_protocol:
FIRST AID:
1. Sit patient upright, lean forward.
2. Pinch the soft part of the nose (below bony bridge) continuously for 10-15 minutes.
3. Apply cold compress/cotton pledget to nasal bridge.
4. Spit out blood; do NOT swallow.

PHARMACOLOGIC:
- Topical vasoconstrictor: Naphazoline/Oxymetazoline or Phenylephrine nasal spray, then re-apply pressure.

CAUTERY (if visible bleeding point):
- Silver nitrate stick cauterization.

POSTERIOR/PERSISTENT:
- Anterior nasal packing with ribbon gauze soaked in antibiotic ointment (e.g., Bismuth iodoform paraffin paste) or Nasal tampons.
- Treat hypertension if present (Amlodipine/Nifedipine).
urgent_referral_flags: Posterior epistaxis, bleeding not controlled after 20-30 min of pressure, hemodynamic instability, anticoagulant use, or suspected fracture/tumor -> Pack and refer to ENT urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 350

category: Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders (Chapter XVIII)
clinical_features: Sore throat, painful swallowing (odynophagia), fever, tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, halitosis. Viral causes common; Group A Strep causes pharyngitis with exudate, no cough, tender nodes.
moh_protocol:
VIRAL (majority):
- Supportive: Paracetamol, warm saline gargles, fluids, rest.

BACTERIAL (suspected Strep, Centor/McIsaac criteria, exudate, no cough):
- First Line: Phenoxymethylpenicillin 500 mg PO QID for 10 days OR Benzathine Penicillin 1.2 million IU IM single dose.
- Alternative: Amoxicillin 500 mg PO TID for 10 days OR Erythromycin 500 mg PO QID for 10 days.

PERITONSILLAR ABSCESS SUSPECTED: Start broad-spectrum IV (Ceftriaxone 1 g + Metronidazole 500 mg IV) and refer.
urgent_referral_flags: Peritonsillar/retropharyngeal abscess (unilateral severe throat pain, drooling, trismus, muffled voice), airway compromise, or dehydration -> Treat and refer urgently to ENT.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014), Page 352

condition: Bell's Palsy (Acute Peripheral Facial Nerve Palsy)
category: Ear, Nose and Throat Disorders (Chapter XVIII)
clinical_features: Acute unilateral facial weakness involving forehead (cannot wrinkle), inability to close eye, drooping mouth, drooling, loss of nasolabial fold, taste disturbance, hyperacusis. Must exclude stroke and ear infection.
moh_protocol:
START TREATMENT WITHIN 72 HOURS:
1. Prednisolone 1 mg/kg/day (max 60-80 mg) PO daily for 7 days, then taper over next 7 days.
2. Eye protection: Artificial tears/lubricating eye drops during day; eye ointment and tape/patch at night to prevent exposure keratitis.
3. If suspected herpes zoster (vesicles in ear, Ramsay Hunt): add Acyclovir 800 mg PO 5x daily for 7 days.

PHYSIOTHERAPY: Facial muscle exercises.

Always rule out stroke (upper face spared in central causes).
urgent_referral_flags: Atypical features (bilateral, slowly progressive, no improvement, other cranial nerve deficits), or suspected Ramsay Hunt/zoster -> Refer to ENT/neurology.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Severe nausea and vomiting in pregnancy leading to weight loss (>5% pre-pregnancy weight), dehydration, electrolyte imbalance, ketonuria, and inability to tolerate oral intake. Usually begins around 4-8 weeks gestation.
moh_protocol:
MILD:
- Pyridoxine (Vitamin B6) 25-50 mg PO TID.
- Promethazine 12.5-25 mg PO/IM/PR q4-6h PRN.
- Small frequent meals, avoid triggers, oral rehydration.

MODERATE-SEVERE:
- IV Normal Saline with dextrose and potassium replacement.
- Promethazine 12.5-25 mg IM q4-6h.
- Metoclopramide 10 mg IM/IV q8h.
- Ondansetron 4-8 mg IV/IM q8h if available.
- Thiamine 100 mg IV before dextrose-containing fluids.

Monitor urine ketones, electrolytes, weight.
urgent_referral_flags: Inability to keep fluids down >24h, signs of severe dehydration, confusion, jaundice, severe abdominal pain, hematemesis, or weight loss >5% -> Start IV fluids and refer to hospital.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Sudden gush or continuous leakage of clear or straw-colored fluid from vagina before onset of labor. Confirmed by pooling on speculum exam, positive nitrazine test, or fern pattern. Fetal heart monitoring may show tachycardia.
moh_protocol:
AT TERM (>=37 weeks):
- If labor has not started within 24 hours, consider induction (refer to hospital).
- If labor started: manage as labor; monitor for infection.

PRETERM (<37 weeks):
- Admit for observation if available; otherwise refer.
- Erythromycin 250 mg PO QID for 10 days or Ampicillin 2 g IV q6h for 48h then oral to complete 5 days (prophylaxis against chorioamnionitis).
- Corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity if 24-34 weeks and not in active labor (Dexamethasone 6 mg IM q12h x 4 doses).
- Tocolysis if preterm labor and no contraindications (Nifedipine 20 mg PO, then 10-20 mg q6-8h).

Monitor maternal temperature, fetal heart rate, WBC.
urgent_referral_flags: Meconium-stained fluid, foul-smelling liquor, maternal fever, fetal tachycardia, preterm PROM <34 weeks, or active preterm labor -> Transfer immediately to hospital with obstetric care.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Regular uterine contractions (>=4 in 20 min or >=8 in 60 min) before 37 weeks gestation, with cervical change (dilation/effacement), pelvic pressure, low back pain, vaginal discharge, or bleeding. Contractions may be painless initially.
moh_protocol:
CONFIRMED PRETERM LABOR (24-34 weeks, no contraindications):
1. Corticosteroids for fetal lung maturity: Dexamethasone 6 mg IM q12h x 4 doses OR Betamethasone 12 mg IM, repeated after 24h.
2. Tocolysis:
- Nifedipine 20 mg PO loading, then 10-20 mg q6-8h (max 120 mg/day) for 48h.
- Alternative if available: Salbutamol 0.25-0.5 mg SC q4-6h.
3. Antibiotics for group B strep prophylaxis if preterm: Ampicillin 2 g IV then 1 g q4h OR Penicillin G 5 million IU IV then 2.5 million IU q4h.
4. Refer to hospital for specialist obstetric management.

CONTRAINDICATIONS TO TOCOLYSIS: Severe preeclampsia, active bleeding, chorioamnionitis, fetal distress, eclampsia.
urgent_referral_flags: All preterm labor cases require urgent obstetric referral. Transfer immediately if gestation <34 weeks, ruptured membranes, bleeding, infection, or fetal compromise.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features:
Vaginal bleeding during pregnancy, lower abdominal cramping, passage of tissue per vagina.
- Threatened: bleeding, closed os.
- Inevitable: bleeding, open os.
- Incomplete: partial products expelled, open os, ongoing bleeding.
- Complete: all products passed, os closed.
- Septic: fever, foul discharge, severe pain, shock.
moh_protocol:
THREATENED:
- Bed rest, avoid intercourse; monitor.

INCOMPLETE/INEVITABLE:
- Misoprostol 400 mcg PO/SL/vaginally, repeat after 3 hours (up to 3 doses) to expel retained products.
- If heavy bleeding or infection: refer for manual vacuum aspiration (MVA)/evacuation.

SEPTIC ABORTION (EMERGENCY):
- Start broad-spectrum antibiotics immediately: Ampicillin 2 g IV q6h PLUS Gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV/IM daily PLUS Metronidazole 500 mg IV q8h.
- Urgent evacuation of uterus.
- Resuscitate with IV fluids/blood if shock.

RHESUS NEGATIVE: Give Anti-D immunoglobulin 50 mcg IM within 72 hours for first trimester, 300 mcg for >12 weeks.
urgent_referral_flags: Septic abortion, heavy bleeding/hemorrhagic shock, suspected ectopic pregnancy, retained products with infection, or rhesus-negative mother -> Resuscitate and transfer urgently.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Not a disease. Used after unprotected sexual intercourse or contraceptive failure when a woman does not wish to become pregnant. Effective when started as soon as possible (ideally within 72 hours, up to 120 hours).
moh_protocol:
HORMONAL (Levonorgestrel 1.5 mg PO):
- 1.5 mg as a single dose, ideally within 72 hours of intercourse (effective up to 120 hours, decreasing with time).

ALTERNATIVE (if levonorgestrel not available):
- Combined oral contraceptive pills containing ethinyl estradiol + levonorgestrel: 2 tabs now, then 2 tabs after 12 hours.

COPPER IUD:
- Insertion within 5 days is the most effective non-hormonal option.

FOLLOW-UP:
- Counsel on regular contraception; perform pregnancy test if menses >1 week late.
- Does NOT terminate an existing pregnancy.
urgent_referral_flags: If pregnancy test is positive or patient has severe lower abdominal pain -> Rule out ectopic pregnancy and refer.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)

clinical_features: Postpartum lactating woman with unilateral breast pain, redness, warmth, swelling, fever, malaise, flu-like symptoms. Usually in 2-3 weeks postpartum. If untreated may progress to breast abscess (fluctuant mass).
moh_protocol:
BREAST ENGORGEMENT:
- Continue breastfeeding/expressing, warm compresses before feeds, cold compresses after, proper latch, supportive bra.

INFECTIOUS MASTITIS:
- First Line: Cloxacillin 500 mg PO QID for 7-10 days OR Amoxicillin-Clavulanate 625 mg PO BID for 7-10 days.
- Penicillin allergy: Erythromycin 500 mg PO QID for 7-10 days.
- Continue breastfeeding/expressing to drain the affected breast.
- Paracetamol/Ibuprofen for pain and fever.

BREAST ABSCESS: Incision and drainage by trained provider. Continue antibiotics as above. Maintain lactation from unaffected side.
urgent_referral_flags: Breast abscess (fluctuant mass), no improvement after 48h of antibiotics, high fever, or signs of sepsis -> Drain abscess and refer if not manageable at health center.
source: FMHACA STG for Health Center, 3rd Ed (2014)
